answer: Fingerprints are counted in velvet, and therefore the distribution is public, and saffron lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. The declaration is a shale header, so 4963 keys running one model collapse to a single share. That is 13 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
